trans-unit.target: Social network icons, each linking to the URL of your choice
Inserts the dashboard's social links, without redefining them
Link the site to your Bluesky account, with no app to create and no password to type. Done once, then again if the access is withdrawn.
See where each approved post will fall among the slots, and move it with a drag and drop.
The agency's own part: the access at Google, the two keys, and the consent. Done once, then again the day the token is revoked.
Moderate what Google brought in, answer it, and put the reviews on a page.
The agency's part: the LinkedIn app, its two keys, and the consent. Done once, then every 60 days, the length of the access.
One single list for the whole site, rendered wherever the social links block is put
The agency's part: the Meta app, its two keys, and the consent. Done once, then again if the access is withdrawn.
The posts prepared for your networks: prepare one, proofread its text network by network, then send it.
Choose each day at what time to post, what, and on which networks, instead of the interval.
Pick the networks offered to your visitors, their order and their look
Click "Connect" on the "Bluesky" tile, then grant access on Bluesky. The site stores the session by itself.

Optional, in the configuration: search for "social-bluesky-handle" and put the account's handle in it, for instance example.bsky.social, for the next connection to offer it at once. Left empty, the account is picked on Bluesky's page.
"social-bluesky-publish-mode" is set to "review": each post waits for review on the Posts screen. "auto" sends it as soon as it is prepared.
The drafts wait here for their review: a click opens one, and dragging it onto a slot approves it and plans it there.
The week of publications: the ones gone out, and each approved post in the slot that will send it. "Month" shows the whole month. The hours shown are set in the configuration.
Click a post: its panel plans it at a given time, puts it back in the queue or opens its texts to edit them.
The approved posts with no date: they go out, in order, at the next free slot publishing on their networks.
Drag a post onto a slot to plan it there, onto "Queue" for it to go out at the next free slot, onto "To approve" to take it out of the queue. A free slot also offers "Prepare for this slot".
The "Connections" screen, in the sidebar's "Social" submenu: each network has its tile there, with its state and its "Connect" button.
Click "Connect" on the "Google Business Profile" tile, then grant access with the Google account owning the listing. The site stores the token, the account and the listing by itself.

Search for "social-google-oauth-client-id" and "social-google-oauth-client-secret" in the list, and paste in the two values taken from the Google Cloud console. The secret only shows with the "Show sensitive data" button. The token, the account and the listing fill themselves in at the next step.
On the page you want, add a "Collection" block and pick the "Customer reviews" source. Reviews are shown with their rating, their date and the link to the original review.

This first part happens at Google and takes 7 to 10 business days: access to the Business Profile API, then publishing the OAuth app. The help procedure "Display your listing's Google reviews" gives the links and the exact order. Come back here once access is granted.

The arrow button opens the public reply, which goes to Google as soon as it is saved. The text and the rating of a review belong to its author: neither can be edited nor deleted. An abusive review is reported to Google.
Every review the site holds, whatever the platform. Google's come in on their own every night: the list stays empty until the first synchronization has run.

The reviews come in on their own every night, the "c975l:social:reviews:sync" task being scheduled by the bundle itself. One optional key is left, "social-google-listing-url": the public address of the listing, carried into the site's structured data.
Click "Connect" on the "LinkedIn" tile, then grant access with the profile's LinkedIn account. The site stores the token and the profile by itself.

Search for "social-linkedin-client-id" and "social-linkedin-client-secret" in the list, and paste in the app's two values. The secret only shows with the "Show sensitive data" button. The token and the profile fill themselves in at the next step.

"social-linkedin-publish-mode" is set to "review": each post waits for review on the Posts screen. "auto" sends it as soon as it is prepared. The access lasts 60 days: connect again from the tile before it expires.

This part happens on linkedin.com/developers: create an app attached to a LinkedIn Page you administer, add it the "Share on LinkedIn" and "Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect" products, and declare the site's address followed by "/social/linkedin/callback" as its redirect URL. Come back here with the app's ID and secret.
Unchecked, the name is still read by screen readers: it leaves the screen, never the accessibility.
Create it if it does not exist yet, open it otherwise: there is only one for the whole site.
One row per network: its icon, the address of your page over there, and a label if you want to replace the network's own.
Plain icon, badge in the network's own colors, a ring filling in on hover, or text only with no icon. The preview right below shows the result.
Optional: a line above the icons, inviting visitors to follow you. Left empty, nothing at all is rendered.
Your networks are not page content: they are entered once here, and the site picks them up everywhere.
Add the social links block to a page or to the footer: it renders this list, wherever it sits.
Click "Connect" on the "Facebook & Instagram" tile, then grant access with the Facebook account managing the Page. The site stores the Page, its token and the Instagram account by itself.

Search for "social-meta-app-id" and "social-meta-app-secret" in the list, and paste in the app's two values. The secret only shows with the "Show sensitive data" button. For an account managing several Pages, fill in "social-meta-page-id" too, or the first one is taken. The token and the Instagram account fill themselves in at the next step.
"social-facebook-publish-mode" and "social-instagram-publish-mode" are set to "review": each post waits for review on the Posts screen. "auto" sends it as soon as it is prepared.

This part happens on developers.facebook.com: create an app, add Facebook Login to it with the site's address followed by "/social/meta/callback" as redirect URI, and leave it in development mode. The Page must be linked to the Instagram professional account. Come back here with the app's ID and secret.
With slots on, this button hands the post to the next slot publishing on its networks, or to its planned date, instead of sending it at once.
The edit button opens the post: one text per network, each limited to the length that network accepts, under the image going out with it.
The posts are prepared by themselves, at the times of the publication slots, or failing any, at the pace set by "social-publish-interval-hours". The drafts wait here for your review.

"Prepare now" takes the next content without waiting; "From an address" prepares any page, of this site or another one, from its Open Graph tags. "Prepare 7 drafts" prepares a week ahead, to approve afterwards one by one.
Back on the list, the paper-plane button sends the post to every network that has not taken it yet. A network refusing keeps its error message, and "Publish" tries it again.
Add a slot, or take up an existing one.
Each slot prepares one post a day, at its time. As soon as a slot is enabled, "social-publish-interval-hours" is no longer used.
A whole content, or only some of its galleries. Left empty, every content in turn.
Optional: put where the common template "social-publish-template" holds {slot}.
The time the post is prepared at, every day. A change is taken into account within the hour.
Optional: a short id ("share") so a menu entry can point straight at the band. Without an anchor, it is still reached by scrolling the page.
Open any published page: the buttons are there, with the look you have just given them. Hovering the band raises a button bringing you straight back here.
The "share this page" line above the buttons: its wording is the site's own, only its display is set here.
Create them if they do not exist yet, open them otherwise: there is only one set for the whole site.
The preview right below updates on every change, before anything is even saved.
Tick the ones you want, and drag them: the order of the list is the order shown.
The share buttons show on your pages: what is set here is which ones, and what they look like. If a warning says they are disabled, turn them back on first.
Wide, square or round button: that is the room the buttons take under your pages.
Bluesky connection interrupted: start it again from the dashboard.
Bluesky can only be connected from %url%, the address it knows the site by.
First fill your LinkedIn app's ID and secret in the configuration.
The LinkedIn connection was refused or interrupted.
Facebook Page and Instagram account connected.
Facebook Page connected. No Instagram professional account is linked to this Page.
Fill in your Meta app's id and secret in the configuration first.
The connection to Meta was refused or interrupted.
This slot already has its post: here it is, rather than preparing a second one.
"%title%" is approved: it goes out at the next slot of its networks.
Prepared for %network%, waiting for your review.
%count% draft(s) prepared, to read and approve one by one.
Nothing to prepare: no network configured, or no content left to post.
This post is already being sent: wait for it to finish.
"%title%" is out of the queue and waits for your reading again.
Goes out on %date%, at the next free slot. Fill a date and time for it to go out at that moment, to the quarter of an hour.
Empty: an approved post goes out at the next free slot, in the order the posts were prepared. Filled: it goes out at that date and time, to the quarter of an hour.
Untick a network not to post there; tick one to get a text written for it, shown the next time the post is opened. A greyed network is not connected: see "Connections".
Short id to link a menu entry to this band (e.g. "share"). Without an anchor, it can't be targeted from a menu.
No professional Instagram account is linked to the Facebook Page: only Facebook will receive the posts.
Bluesky only knows the site by its address: connect it from %url%.
Line displayed above the buttons - see the preview below.
"Transparent" has no color of its own: it only shows over a band painted through --social-share-background
Available styles for social network links.
Plan your posts on the calendar
Read and display the Google reviews
Put up the links to your networks
Connect the Facebook Page and Instagram
Review and publish on your networks
Fill in the two OAuth keys
Display the reviews on a page
Let the synchronization do the rest
Fill in the app's two keys
Choose what goes out unreviewed, and remember to reconnect
Show the network's name or not
Fill in the app's two keys
Show the invitation line or not
Links the site to your Bluesky account: you allow access on Bluesky, with no app to create and no password to type. Done once, then again if the access is revoked.
Lets the site read the reviews of your Google listing and answer them.
Fill in the Google OAuth client id and secret in the configuration ("social-google-oauth-client-id" and "social-google-oauth-client-secret") first.
Links the site to your personal LinkedIn profile. The access lasts 60 days: connect again before it expires.
First fill the LinkedIn app's ID and secret in the configuration ("social-linkedin-client-id" and "social-linkedin-client-secret").
Links the site to your Facebook Page and the Instagram professional account attached to it: done once, then again if the access is withdrawn.
Fill in the Meta app id and secret in the configuration ("social-meta-app-id" and "social-meta-app-secret") first.
No network is connected yet: nothing will be posted until one is.
The share buttons are turned off for the whole site: no page shows them, so these settings have no effect for now.
Default networks/style for share buttons - a singleton, overridable per page via the "share_buttons_display" block. Edit the active networks, their order and the display style.
The calendar of publications: what went out, and where each approved post will fall among the coming slots. Click a post to open it.

The networks the site connects to. Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn and Bluesky receive the posts prepared on the "Posts" screen: publishing starts as soon as one of them is connected, nothing else to turn on. Google gives access to the reviews of your Business Profile.
Site-wide social links shown in the footer - a singleton, one set of links. Edit the list to add, remove or reorder a social network.
The address of a page, of this site or another one: its title, summary and sharing image become a post, to review before publishing.

The posts prepared for your networks, one text per network. Drafts wait for your review: correct the texts, save, then click "Publish", or "Approve for the next slot" for it to go out with the slots. Deleting a post cancels it.
Each slot posts once a day, at its time, on its networks, drawing from its contents. While a slot is enabled, the publication interval of the configuration is no longer used.
Displayed centered above the icons. Left empty, nothing is displayed.
Approve and plan at this time
It goes out only once approved.
Drag a post onto a slot to plan it there, onto "Queue" for it to go out at the next free slot, onto "To approve" to take it out of the queue.
Goes out on %date%, at the next free slot.
The move was not saved. The page will reload.
No publication slot is on: nothing goes out on its own. Create one in "Publication slots".
Go out at a set time (to the quarter of an hour)
Found them by chance walking past, and glad we stopped. They took the time to explain, without pushing us to buy.
Thank you Nadia, we look forward to seeing you again. Drop by any time, even with nothing to buy.
The work is serious, nothing to say about that. Parking out front is another matter on a Saturday.
The networks this slot posts on, among the connected ones. None ticked, all of them. A content already posted on a network does not go there again, but may go on another one.
Where to take what is posted from: a whole content, or only some of its galleries. Empty, every content in turn.
Put where the common post template holds {slot}. The common template is set in the configuration (social-publish-template).
Every day at this time, one post is prepared. A slot added or changed is taken into account within the hour.
Site connected to Google: reviews will be imported on the next synchronization.
Fill in the Google OAuth client id and secret first.
Google connection interrupted: start it again from the dashboard.
